2608.26235.title: The Reasoning Tax: Token Economics of LLM Reasoning Across Task Types and Deployment Contexts
2608.26235.paper_summary: Accuracy-only benchmarking of reasoning-capable large language models misses a central deployment question: when do extended thinking tokens earn their cost? We introduce the Token Economy Score (TES), a marginal benchmarking metric that measures the accuracy gain of a reasoning model over a non-reasoning baseline, normalized by the generated-token multiplier. We define paired and approximated TES variants for model families with reasoning toggles and frontier models without direct non-reasoning counterparts. We then conduct an empirical benchmarking analysis across 151 model-benchmark evaluation runs on seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, science reasoning, instruction following, expert knowledge, knowledge recall, and research-level physics. The analysis examines three deployment-facing dimensions: which task structures yield positive marginal reasoning efficiency, how increasing reasoning effort changes TES within model families, and how deployment context changes economic viability. Results show that task structure predicts reasoning efficiency better than nominal difficulty: sequential inferencechain tasks such as AIME 2025 and LiveCodeBench show high TES, while knowledge-recall tasks such as MMLU-Pro show low TES despite their difficulty. We also find systematic diminishing returns at higher reasoning effort levels, including cases where additional thinking reduces accuracy. Finally, Reasoning Cost Share (RCS) shows that inference spend is often dominated by internal thinking, while Deployment Cost Multiplier (DCM) shows how on-premises deployment can change the economics of otherwise costly reasoning workloads. These findings support a benchmarking-driven model-selection rule: enable reasoning selectively by task type, effort level, and deployment context rather than treating it as a universally beneficial mode.
2608.26235.paper_summary_zh: 準確性僅基準的推理能力大型語言模型忽略了一個核心的部署問題：何時擴展思考令牌能夠賺回其成本？我們引入了令牌經濟分數（Token Economy Score, TES），這是一種邊際基準指標，用於衡量推理模型相對於非推理基準的準確性增益，並以生成令牌的倍數進行標準化。我們為具有推理切換的模型家族和沒有直接非推理對應的前沿模型定義了配對和近似的 TES 變體。然後，我們在七個基準上進行了151次模型基準評估運行的實證基準分析，這些基準涵蓋了數學、代碼生成、科學推理、指令跟隨、專家知識、知識回憶和研究級物理。該分析考察了三個面向部署的維度：哪些任務結構產生正的邊際推理效率、增加推理努力如何改變模型家族中的 TES，以及部署上下文如何改變經濟可行性。結果顯示，任務結構比名義難度更好地預測推理效率：如 AIME 2025 和 LiveCodeBench 等序列推理鏈任務顯示出高 TES，而如 MMLU-Pro 等知識回憶任務儘管難度較高卻顯示出低 TES。我們還發現，在更高的推理努力水平下，系統性地出現邊際收益遞減的情況，包括額外思考會降低準確性的情況。最後，推理成本份額（Reasoning Cost Share, RCS）顯示推理支出通常被內部思考所主導，而部署成本倍數（Deployment Cost Multiplier, DCM）則顯示本地部署如何改變原本昂貴的推理工作負載的經濟學。這些發現支持了一個基於基準的模型選擇規則：根據任務類型、努力水平和部署上下文選擇性地啟用推理，而不是將其視為一種普遍有益的模式。
